title: tenant-scoped-roles-and-audit-ingest-checklist-v2
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact, deployment-aware IAM role matrix, minimal policy templates, an audit-log schema tailored for SIEM ingestion, and a checklist for evidence automation pipelines. Goal: give engineering and security teams a reproducible starting point for enforcing RBAC v2 across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while ensuring audit telemetry is SIEM-ready.

Scope and constraints:
- Covers roles scoped by tenant, deployment-mode, and service boundary (control-plane vs runtime).
- Focus on least-privilege role definitions that are simple to reason about and can be automated via policy templates and infra-as-code.
- Assumes existing identity provider (OIDC/SAML) provides subject attributes: user_email, groups, tenant_id, deployment_tier.
- This doc is a draft for cross-team review; it intentionally trades some granularity for deployable clarity.

High-level RBAC v2 approach (summary):
- Role = named collection of permissions + scope attributes (tenant_id, deployment_tier).
- Policy enforcement is attribute-based: allow if (principal.tenant_id == resource.tenant_id) AND (principal.deployment_tier in resource.allowed_tiers).
- Prefer tenant-scoped roles for multi-tenant Hosted; prefer org-scoped roles for Dedicated/Private with delegation hooks.

Recommended role naming convention (stable strings):
- r_<deployment>-<scope>-<persona> e.g. r_hosted_tenant_admin, r_dedicated_infra_readonly, r_private_support_onsite
- persona examples: tenant_admin, app_owner, infra_operator, observability_reader, billing_agent, security_auditor

Compact role matrix (one-line readable rows):
- r_hosted_tenant_admin: deployment=hosted, scope=tenant, permissions=[tenant.users.*, tenant.models.*, tenant.config.*], intended=product teams owning a tenant, require MFA, restrict to group:tenant-admins
- r_hosted_observability_reader: deployment=hosted, scope=tenant, permissions=[telemetry.read, audit.logs.read], intended=SRE/CS for support, read-only, limit to requestable time ranges > 90d only via audit process
- r_dedicated_infra_operator: deployment=dedicated, scope=org, permissions=[cluster.scale, node.replace, model.deploy], intended=customer infra team + Redwood infra on-call, requires VPN and JIT access, IP allowlist
- r_private_support_onsite: deployment=private, scope=customer-site, permissions=[support.ssh_proxy, debug.logs.read], intended=Redwood support for on-prem engagements, ephemeral key material, HSM-derived short-lived creds
- r_security_auditor: deployment=all, scope=read-only-global, permissions=[audit.logs.search, evidence.export], intended=security team, require dedicated audit-role binding and justification ticket

Minimal policy templates (pseudocode, copy/paste friendly):
- Tenant-scoped read-only:
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["models.describe","inference.usage.read","audit.logs.read"],
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"principal:tenant_id": "resource:tenant_id"}}

- Org-level infra modifications (Dedicated):
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["infra.cluster.scale","infra.node.replace"],
  "Condition": {"Bool": {"principal:in_vpn": "true"}, "IpAddress": {"principal.source_ip": "203.0.113.0/24"}}

- Private support ephemeral grant (short TTL):
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["support.ssh_proxy","debug.session.start"],
  "Condition": {"DateLessThan": {"principal:expires": "2025-02-14T12:00:00Z"}, "StringEquals": {"principal:approved_ticket": "JIRA-<id>"}}

Audit log schema (flattened fields for SIEM):
- timestamp: RFC3339 string
- event_id: UUID
- principal_id: opaque id (prefer stable subject id)
- principal_email: human email (if available)
- principal_groups: semicolon-separated list
- principal_tenant: tenant_id or org_id
- principal_attrs: semicolon kv pairs e.g. "mfa=true;location=us-west"
- action: canonical action string (models.deploy, inference.request, audit.export)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, policy, secret
- resource_id: opaque id
- resource_tenant: tenant_id
- deployment_tier: hosted|dedicated|private
- result: success|failure|denied
- outcome_code: numeric or short string error code
- request_id: tracing id to link to trace sampling
- request_latency_ms: integer
- source_ip: IPv4/6 or NATed IP
- auth_method: oidc|saml|api_key|hsm
- policy_evaluation: short summary (allow/deny + rule id)
- evidence_refs: semicolon list of artifact ids (s3 paths, zips)
- raw_payload_snippet: base64 or truncated text (opt-in, privacy-aware)

Example SIEM-ready event (single-line compact JSON for illustration):
{"timestamp":"2025-02-14T11:08:22Z","event_id":"2b4f7c18-8f3a-4e6a-b1e0-9a0d2a3f6c4e","principal_email":"eng-lead@customer.com","principal_tenant":"cust-42","action":"models.deploy","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"m-9123","deployment_tier":"dedicated","result":"denied","outcome_code":"policy.blocked:scoped_mismatch","request_id":"r-7b9d","request_latency_ms":128,"source_ip":"198.51.100.12","auth_method":"oidc","policy_evaluation":"deny:rule-tenant-scope","evidence_refs":"s3://redwood-audit/cust-42/deploy-deny-2b4f7c18.log"}

SIEM export mapping guidance (columns to enforce on ingest):
- Ensure timestamp -> event_time (indexing), principal_tenant -> customer.keyword, deployment_tier -> deployment.keyword, action -> action.keyword, result -> outcome.keyword
- Map request_id to trace_id for cross-system correlation
- Normalize IPs to source.ip field for geolocation and enrichment
- Store policy_evaluation.rule_id as policy.rule_id for drilldowns

Evidence automation checklist (pipeline orientation):
1) Trigger: on deny or on high-severity allow (e.g., admin writes) create evidence job.
2) Capture artifacts: full audit event, relevant logs (service logs +/- 2 minutes), sampled request/response, associated trace/span, IAM policy snapshot, ticket link.
3) Package: TAR with manifest.json listing items and checksums, include minimal PII redaction step.
4) Store: write to immutable bucket path: s3://evidence/YYYY/MM/DD/<event_id>.tar.gz with object lock and MFA delete for retention requirements.
5) TL;DR: Attach evidence_refs to the original audit event and push to SIEM as enrichment field.
6) Retention: standard evidence retention 1 year for low-risk, 7 years for regulated customers (config per-customer).
7) Auto-notify: create a ticket in intake queue (JIRA-SEC-<id>) for security review on high severity.

Automation queries and sample detection rules (for SIEM):
- Rule: Tenant privilege escalation
  Query: events where action in ("iam.grant","roles.bind") AND principal_tenant != resource_tenant AND result=="success"
  Response: create evidence job + suspend subject token via SCIM revoke API (if supported) + notify security slack channel

- Rule: Cross-deployment model pull
  Query: events where action=="models.pull" AND deployment_tier=="private" AND principal.deployment_tier!="private"
  Response: immediate deny + evidence + ticket

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Hosted environments must keep tenant_id present on every audit event; missing tenant_id should be treated as a telemetry ingestion error (alert SRE).
- For Dedicated, privileged actions should require an additional justification attribute (justification_ticket) recorded in the audit event to be admissible as evidence.
- Private/on-prem deployments: where SIEM export is customer-hosted, provide a local exporter that translates our audit schema to the customer SIEM canonical fields; keep exporter code permissively licensed for customers to adapt.
- Be careful with raw_payload_snippet: by default redact prompt/response content for hosted inference unless customer consents.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- eng/serving-runtime: implement tenant_id propagation into event envelope (owner: Miguel Ortega) - due 2024-12-15
- platform-engineering: add policy templates to infra-as-code repo and parameterize TTL for ephemeral grants (owner: Clara Wu) - due 2025-01-10
- security: draft retention/immutable storage controls and review legal requirements for regulated customers (owner: Aisha Patel) - due 2025-01-20
- observability: add SIEM mapping test-suite (sample events + ingestion assertions) (owner: Ravi Desai) - due 2025-01-30

Open questions for doc review:
- Do we want a separate long-lived auditor role across tenants for hosted, or constrain cross-tenant auditing to a request/approval flow? (tradeoff: simplicity vs blast radius)
- Should all deny events auto-trigger evidence collection, or only denies on admin-level actions?
- For private deployments, what is the minimal set of telemetry we require to be enabled to support post-incident analysis without violating customer isolation expectations?

Appendix: brief checklist for onboarding a new customer deployment mode:
- Hosted: ensure tenant_id in auth token, bind tenant_admin group, enable standard SIEM export to central collector, configure evidence bucket with object lock.
- Dedicated: configure org-level infra_operator bindings, apply IP allowlist for infra actions, enable just-in-time approvals and justification ticket enforcement.
- Private: deliver local exporter binary + docs, set guidance for which audit fields must be turned on, provide secure channel for evidence handoff (SFTP or signed upload) when required.

Notes to reviewers: this document is intentionally concise. Please comment inline with prioritization and operational constraints. After consensus we will split into: (1) policy templates repo PR, (2) SIEM mapping spec, (3) evidence automation runbook.
